base_member_text: [L13-L29,L88-L100] (MED/pointer-state) parameter pointer components have no default NULL initialization, and getkey associates only the pointer matching the current type, leaving the other pointer components with undefined or stale association state.

[L13-L19,L88-L100] (LOW/incomplete-metadata) The exported parameter type advertises units, description, and dimension metadata, but getkey initializes none of those fields for a successful scalar lookup.
audit_member_text: [L21-L28] (LOW/undefined pointer state) parameter pointer components have no default NULL() association, leaving unused components undefined or stale across descriptor reuse.

[L88-L100] (MED/incomplete result metadata) Successful getkey calls set only name, rank, type, and one value pointer, leaving the public units, description, dimensions, and nonselected pointer fields undefined or inherited from a previous use.

adversarial.rationale: These are tagged alternatives, not a collection of pointers whose association status must all be valid: successful getkey sets value%type and the corresponding scalar pointer (getkey.F90:L87-L100). The general consumer branches on that tag, and typed getters consume their matching scalar immediately, so unused components remaining undefined does not establish this defect.

base_member_text: [L76-L100] (MED/aliasing-contract) All returned scalar pointers alias one of three shared SAVE temporaries, so a later getkey call of the same type silently changes the value observed through every earlier result and makes the API non-reentrant.
audit_member_text: [L76-L100] (MED/shared-result aliasing) Every getkey result of a given type points to one module-saved scratch scalar, so a later call silently changes the value observed through all earlier descriptors and the routine is not reentrant or thread-safe.

adversarial.rationale: getkey explicitly uses one saved target per scalar type and returns pointers to it; the comment acknowledges the aliasing but does not prevent it. Immediate-copy consumers avoid the problem, yet retaining two successful same-type descriptors through the public getkey API reproduces it.
